title: Distillation Defenses Easily Break After Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2609.35699v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Distillation attacks copy the reasoning capabilities of closed-source large language models, allowing bad actors to replicate state-of-the-art performance at low cost. Attackers systematically collect a large volume of frontier model reasoning traces and then train (i.e., "distill") their own models on these traces. Existing defenses against distillation attacks are typically evaluated immediately after distillation, implicitly assuming attackers do not train their models any further. In this paper, we argue that a more realistic threat model includes further training with reinforcement learning after distillation. A misspecified threat model can give a false sense of security -- some defenses that seem effective after distillation can be broken after subsequent reinforcement learning. translated_title: 蒸馏防御在强化学习之后容易被击破
translated_abstract: 蒸馏攻击会复制闭源大语言模型的推理能力，使恶意攻击者能够以低成本复现最先进的性能。攻击者会系统性地收集大量前沿模型的推理轨迹，然后在这些轨迹上训练（即“蒸馏”）自己的模型。现有的针对蒸馏攻击的防御通常在蒸馏之后立即进行评估，这隐含地假设攻击者不会再进一步训练其模型。在本文中，我们认为一个更现实的威胁模型应当包含蒸馏之后通过强化学习进行的进一步训练。错误设定的威胁模型可能带来虚假的安全感——某些在蒸馏之后看似有效的防御，在随后的强化学习之后可能被轻易击破。在实际中，强化学习降低了蒸馏攻击生效的门槛。我们证明简单的攻击即可窃取推理能力（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文指出仅基于蒸馏后评估的防御机制存在缺陷，证明攻击者在蒸馏后再进行强化学习即可轻易击破这些看似有效的防御，因此更现实的威胁模型必须考虑蒸馏后的进一步训练。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that distillation defenses evaluated only immediately after distillation can be easily broken when attackers perform subsequent reinforcement learning, calling for a more realistic threat model that accounts for post-distillation training.
